title: Primary-source evidence review for independent ETF long/cash research
scope: Fifteen targeted primary academic/institutional sources: the initial twelve plus Faber, RiskMetrics and Lo for actually implemented v3 controls. Evidence review only; no fitting or reserved-performance inspection.
selection_method: Foundational works on momentum, volatility management, implementation costs, predictive modeling and research multiplicity, including counterevidence. This is a scoped evidence map rather than an exhaustive systematic review or a search for guaranteed high returns.
main_assessment: The strongest immediate improvement is a cleaner experiment: separate directional prediction, exposure/volatility management and transaction costs, then subject a small declared hypothesis set to the existing chronological workflow. Literature motivates tests; it does not establish that these 15 ETF accounts will beat buy-and-hold.

already_tested_or_present.item: CART primary; bounded RF and XGBoost challengers
already_tested_or_present.state: Already implemented and compared on saved CART-selected recipes; 2021–2022 matched inner diagnostics also present. No literature-driven promotion implied.

40 eligible numerical features already include multi-horizon momentum, moving-average trends, volatility and peer relationships. Standalone trend controls are different comparisons, not a newly discovered factor.
Already in earlier-fold selection and matched reported sizing sensitivities. One EWMA alternative and passive-with-identical-sizing control are proposed additions.
Already considered in the v2 recipe screen; repeating this same grid is not an additional evidence contribution.
Already reported; a turnover buffer or partial adjustment would change the trade policy and must be a new logged experiment.
Macro diagnostic columns and real local news sentiment demonstrations exist. Historical model eligibility remains gated on source vintages/versions and historical availability.

protocol_constraints.reserved_policy: No 2024+ selection, fitting, forecasting, performance inspection or scoring for these proposed hypotheses.
protocol_constraints.scope: Independent instrument long/cash only; no portfolio allocation, shorting, leverage, options or RL.
protocol_constraints.timing: Last completed weekly close decision, next actual session open; preprocessing/calibration/selection trained earlier; purge actual overlapping label intervals and use matured outcomes.
protocol_constraints.selection: The same historical outer results cannot choose a new winning hypothesis and then serve as its untouched confirmation. Any promotion procedure must itself be fixed and nested earlier.
protocol_constraints.primary_metric: Net daily Sharpe difference relative to each ETF buy/hold under identical dates, costs and cash/risk-free conventions; also compare against identical-sizing passive controls.
protocol_constraints.multiplicity: Count every tried specification and record unsuccessful variants. More hypotheses increase the evidence burden rather than automatically increasing confidence.
protocol_constraints.implemented_v3_menu: Sixteen IDs documented in v3_hypothesis_evidence.json; some original review suggestions remain unimplemented. All result fields in the evidence mapping stay null.

papers.title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; author/institution-hosted October 2016 version read
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; introduction; Section I.B portfolio formation and I.C methodology; pp. 1–10 of hosted PDF
papers.finding: Prior realized variance inversely scales monthly factor exposure. Studied factors show improved risk-adjusted performance because their expected returns do not rise proportionately with volatility.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Inverse variance differs from this system's inverse-volatility cap. Factor portfolios, leverage, cash and scaling conventions differ from an unlevered weekly single-ETF account.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Compare fixed exposure, existing volatility sizing, and passive exposure with identical sizing; keep normalization based exclusively on prior data.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Time Series Momentum
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; AQR research summary and Yale-hosted published PDF read
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; Section 2.4 ex-ante volatility; Section 3 strategy construction; https://fairmodel.econ.yale.edu/ec439/mosk.pdf
papers.finding: Across 58 futures and forwards, own past returns exhibit continuation over roughly one to twelve months. The strategy combines return signs with lagged volatility scaling.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Evidence uses diversified, often leveraged long/short futures. ETF long/cash removes shorts, changes carry and costs, and may weaken the result.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Predeclare a 252-session own-return-sign long/cash control and evaluate its fixed and volatility-sized versions separately.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: … and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; author-hosted published PDF
papers.finding: A large literature of tested factors requires stronger significance standards than isolated tests; the authors derive thresholds reflecting extensive factor searches.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Their often-cited t-statistic hurdle is not a universal cutoff for weekly ETF timing. Correlation, hidden trials and overlapping labels matter here.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Log every tried rule and report search-adjusted evidence across the declared hypothesis family, including failures.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
papers.publication: The Journal of Portfolio Management 40(5), 94–107, Special 40th Anniversary Issue
papers.source_type: Academic/practitioner journal article; author-hosted paper and publisher metadata
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; multiple-testing and DSR sections; Appendix 3 on implied independent trials
papers.finding: DSR adjusts a selected Sharpe statistic for multiple searching, sample length and non-normal returns, using information about the distribution and dependence of trials.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Unknown prior searches, serial dependence and uncertain effective trial counts make a mechanical DSR confidence claim unreliable; raw configuration count is not independence.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Add a sensitivity diagnostic over plausible effective trial counts; disclose missing earlier searches and retain dependence-aware uncertainty.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; institutional repository and February 2015 author preprint read
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; holdout discussion; CSCV construction and limitations; https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf
papers.finding: The authors propose combinatorially symmetric cross-validation to estimate how often an in-sample winner ranks below the median on the complementary selection subset.
papers.limits_for_this_project: CSCV is an overfitting diagnostic, not chronological deployment validation. Partitioning dependent returns and omitting unsuccessful trials can distort its interpretation.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Use a complete pre-2024 candidate-return matrix for a secondary stability diagnostic while retaining purged forward chronological model evaluation.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Backtesting Strategies Based on Multiple Signals
papers.source_type: Institutional academic working paper; NBER full abstract read
papers.reviewed_content: NBER abstract; 2016 NBER program confirms a related presentation titled Testing Strategies Based on Multiple Signals
papers.finding: Selecting and signing multiple signals can generate severe overfitting even from random inputs. Searching signal combinations compounds ordinary multiple-testing bias.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Cross-sectional stock-selection experiments do not numerically calibrate ETF timing bias. The warning nevertheless applies to feature subsets, signs, thresholds and regime combinations.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Test a few economic blocks through predeclared ablations rather than exhaustively combining all forty primary features.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; September 13, 2019 author version and author publication page
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; estimation/validation discussion; Section 3 empirical split; appendix temporal evaluation scheme
papers.finding: Nonlinear interactions help tree and neural models in a large stock panel; momentum, liquidity and volatility remain influential. Tuning and testing use separated chronological samples.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Thousands of stocks and decades of monthly panel observations differ sharply from one ETF's weekly samples; this is not evidence that larger networks improve this project.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Keep CART, bounded RF/XGB, and one regularized linear control on matched folds; fit all scaling and tuning within earlier samples.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: A Comprehensive Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; publisher full abstract and metadata read
papers.reviewed_content: Publisher abstract only; no claim to have reviewed inaccessible full journal text
papers.finding: Many proposed aggregate equity-premium predictors performed poorly out of sample and exhibited unstable relationships, undermining the market-timing benefit implied by in-sample fits.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Aggregate equity-premium regressions do not settle every ETF or nonlinear method. Their historical-average benchmark remains a useful low-complexity hurdle.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Compare forecast errors with a prior matured historical-mean forecast, alongside identical-date buy/hold and passive volatility-sized trading controls.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; Harvard institutional repository full abstract and metadata read
papers.reviewed_content: Repository abstract; sign and forecast restrictions described there
papers.finding: Economically motivated restrictions on coefficient signs and forecasts allow some predictive regressions to improve upon historical-average forecasts, although explanatory gains remain small.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Equity-premium sign restrictions need not hold for Treasury, commodity or sector ETF returns. The paper does not validate this project's specific calibration or shrinkage rule.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Test one shrink-to-prior conditional-payoff estimate using earlier matured cross-fitted predictions; predeclare restrictions instead of choosing them after outer results.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; author-hosted published PDF
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; introduction; structural-instability analysis and Table 9; conclusion
papers.finding: Across 103 equity strategies, volatility-managed portfolios do not systematically win direct comparisons. Implementable out-of-sample combinations often disappoint because the spanning relations are unstable.
papers.limits_for_this_project: This does not prove all volatility control useless. It challenges universal performance claims and full-sample spanning allocations, rather than this exact capped ETF implementation.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Retain unmanaged and identical-sizing passive controls; estimate every allocation parameter earlier and report subperiod stability and turnover.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; author/institution-hosted published PDF
papers.reviewed_content: Abstract; introduction; Sections I–III, especially quadratic costs and partial trading
papers.finding: In a dynamic model with costly trading and decaying forecasts, gradual adjustment toward a forward-looking target balances expected gains against turnover; persistent signals merit greater weight.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Its quadratic-cost, model-based multiasset solution is not an optimality proof for ETF deadbands under proportional costs. A simple buffer or partial trade is an adaptation.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Test one fixed partial-rebalance fraction or one weight buffer, holding signals constant; measure net benefit against foregone gross returns.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: Time Series Momentum and Volatility Scaling
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; publisher abstract/introduction/conclusion excerpts and author-institution metadata
papers.reviewed_content: Publisher full abstract plus indexed introduction/conclusion; UMSL author record verifies DOI/authors; full journal PDF not accessed
papers.finding: In their futures reexamination, much apparent time-series-momentum performance is associated with volatility scaling; scaled and unscaled passive comparisons materially change the interpretation.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Their sample and specifications do not invalidate every trend rule. They show why scaling and directional timing must be isolated before attributing gains.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Use the two-by-two control: passive versus momentum, each at fixed exposure and with identical causal volatility sizing.
papers.hypothesis_status: Our proposed adaptation; not a profitability claim or exact replication

papers.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
papers.publication: The Journal of Wealth Management 9(4), 69–79, Spring 2007
papers.source_type: Academic/practitioner journal article; author-hosted February 2013 update read, not claimed original 2007 full text
papers.reviewed_content: Updated abstract; Step 2 model definition and assumptions, PDF pp. 19–22; Step 3 portfolio interpretation, pp. 29–33; original journal metadata verified separately
papers.finding: The simple rule holds an asset above its ten-month moving average and otherwise cash. Historical multiasset/index tests emphasize risk reduction and lower drawdowns.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Source updates monthly, assumes signal-close fills and Treasury-bill cash, and initially excludes trading frictions. Weekly next-open ETF execution and zero-cash accounting differ.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Use the completed-month ten-month signal as a fixed control; separately test capped volatility sizing under identical dates and costs.
papers.hypothesis_status: Adaptation in trend_10m_fixed/trend_10m_vol; not an exact replication or return guarantee

papers.title: RiskMetrics—Technical Document, Fourth Edition
papers.publication: J.P. Morgan/Reuters institutional technical document, December 1996
papers.source_type: Primary institutional methodology document, preserved by MSCI; not an academic alpha study
papers.reviewed_content: Cover/preface; Chapter 5 EWMA recursion, Sections 5.2–5.3; Table 5.9; printed pp. 81–100 (PDF pp. 92–112)
papers.finding: RiskMetrics specifies recursively weighted squared returns with zero sample mean, using daily decay 0.94 and monthly decay 0.97 for its volatility and correlation forecasts.
papers.limits_for_this_project: This estimates risk, not expected returns or trading alpha. Arithmetic ETF returns, warmup, weekly sizing and exposure caps are implementation choices beyond the document's daily estimator.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Use fixed daily lambda 0.94 as one causal volatility estimator, holding the baseline signal and risk bounds constant.
papers.hypothesis_status: Estimator/parameter provenance for ewma_vol; strategy performance remains unestablished

papers.title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
papers.source_type: Academic journal article; CFA Institute publisher and MIT author full abstracts/metadata read
papers.reviewed_content: Complete publisher and author abstracts; full subscription article not claimed as read
papers.finding: Sharpe estimation and time aggregation depend on return-generating assumptions. Serial correlation can materially alter annualization, uncertainty and apparent performance rankings.
papers.limits_for_this_project: Lo does not prescribe this project's twenty-session block length or establish bootstrap validity after its adaptive search. Serial dependence and nonstationarity still require sensitivity analysis.
papers.implementable_hypothesis: Retain clearly labeled convention-based Sharpe and paired dependence-aware uncertainty; test robustness to dependence assumptions before interpreting differences as evidence.
papers.hypothesis_status: Inference support across all v3 comparisons; no alpha prediction or fixed resampling-parameter endorsement

finite_controls.name: Separate trend timing from volatility sizing
finite_controls.status: new standalone controls; momentum inputs already exist
finite_controls.specification: A fixed two-by-two: always-long and sign(C_t/C_(t-252)-1)>0, each with fixed weight and existing capped 63-session volatility sizing. Use weekly completed-close decisions and next-open execution; no negative weights.
finite_controls.declared_choices: One 252-session lookback; existing 10% annual volatility target, 5% volatility floor and 100% exposure cap. No extra optimization or inverse-variance substitution.
finite_controls.comparison: Same instrument, same common eligible dates, same cost/cash convention. Report timing gain relative to passive with the SAME sizing and total gain relative to buy/hold.

finite_controls.name: One EWMA volatility alternative
finite_controls.status: Implemented v3 uses RiskMetrics lambda 0.94, superseding the initial optional 60/61 suggestion
finite_controls.specification: Actual ewma_vol uses squared daily arithmetic returns, EWMA lambda=0.94, adjust=False and minimum 20 returns, annualized at 252; the original baseline signal and 10% target/5% floor/100% cap remain fixed.
finite_controls.declared_choices: Use the fixed v3 declaration. RiskMetrics motivates the daily 0.94 estimator, not ETF performance, minimum-history choice or the earlier unimplemented 60/61 alternative.
finite_controls.comparison: Hold the directional signal fixed; compare realized volatility tracking error, net Sharpe, turnover and downside losses versus existing vol63 sizing.
finite_controls.original_optional_specification: Use one fixed exponential decay, lambda=60/61, motivated by the source's 60-day center of mass; annualize at 252 and keep existing no-leverage sizing bounds. Specify initialization, centered variance and minimum 63 valid returns before evaluation.

finite_controls.name: Cost-aware target adjustment
finite_controls.specification: Choose ONE policy before evaluating: partial adjustment w_new=w_current+0.5*(w_target-w_current), or a fixed 0.10 absolute-weight deadband. Use actual drifted current holdings and preserve bounds [0,1].
finite_controls.declared_choices: If both policies are tried, count two separate hypotheses. Do not describe either heuristic as the paper's proven optimum. Never choose after reading the same outer interval.
finite_controls.comparison: Same forecasts and target weights; evaluate turnover savings, costs, slower exits and foregone gross returns at 0/5/10 bps one-way.

finite_controls.name: Bounded regularized linear control
finite_controls.status: new model comparator; CART/RF/XGB already compared
finite_controls.specification: One standardized ridge regression baseline with alpha=1 and a five-session net-return target, using the technical block only. Training-only scaling; annual forward refit; no feature/hyperparameter tournament.
finite_controls.declared_choices: A single explicit control; any alternative horizon, feature block or regularization parameter creates another logged trial. Compare matched labels and folds, not a hand-picked favorable date range.
finite_controls.comparison: Historical-mean forecast error, calibration where applicable, and net trading Sharpe on matched exposure/date conventions.

finite_controls.name: Shrink conditional payoff before position decisions
finite_controls.status: new later-stage sizing/gating hypothesis; not established by cited paper
finite_controls.specification: Estimate conditional payoff from earlier matured chronological cross-fitted forecasts and outcomes, then shrink it 50% toward the earlier unconditional mean. Keep the horizon consistent and separate any uncertainty/sizing choice from win probability.
finite_controls.declared_choices: Fix shrinkage at 0.5 for the first comparison; calibrate only in earlier folds. Avoid counting the current label hurdle twice when comparing expected net payoff with switching costs.
finite_controls.comparison: Prior-only reliability, squared forecast error, net benefit after turnover, and stability of estimated payoff; do not map an uncalibrated win probability directly to weight.

finite_controls.name: Account for the expanded search
finite_controls.status: required evidence discipline, not a new alpha signal
finite_controls.specification: Create an immutable hypothesis ledger before computation; preserve all losing trials, parameter changes, evaluation dates and promotion decisions. Distinguish diagnostic resamples from chronological model fits.
finite_controls.declared_choices: Record raw trial count and dependence assumptions. DSR sensitivity and development-only PBO may supplement, not replace, purged expanding-window evaluation and prospective validation.
finite_controls.comparison: Show the full search distribution and rank stability. Do not treat 15 correlated ETF results or repeated engineering reruns as independent replications.

finite_controls.name: Respect information availability and source boundaries
finite_controls.specification: Keep 2024+ reserved; use no reserved performance to tune these hypotheses. Existing latest-vintage macro and current RSS/FinBERT demonstrations stay excluded until original-vintage/version/availability histories are qualified.
finite_controls.declared_choices: Any feature, calibration, threshold or trade policy selected after inspecting 2008–2023 performance is exploratory for that inspected interval, even if predictions were generated chronologically.
finite_controls.comparison: Historical developmental evidence first; freeze the complete selection procedure before any separately authorized reserve test, and distinguish previously seen reserve history from a genuinely prospective period.

finite_controls.name: Keep cash and benchmark conventions identical
finite_controls.status: measurement sensitivity, not an asserted trading improvement
finite_controls.specification: Current results use zero cash/risk-free return. A later audited cash-yield sensitivity must credit identical available cash rates across all accounts and compute excess-return Sharpe consistently.
finite_controls.declared_choices: Do not treat an annual percent bill quote as a decimal daily return, or silently replace zero-cash results. Historical rate availability and discount-basis conversion require an explicit contract.
finite_controls.comparison: Separate changes due to idle-cash carry, average exposure, timing and costs; lower volatility alone is not evidence of predictive alpha.

interpretation_checks: Risk-adjusted improvement is different from a higher CAGR; neither establishes causal predictive alpha without appropriate exposure/risk controls.
Inverse variance, inverse volatility, leveraged risk normalization and unlevered capped volatility targeting are distinct strategies.
A favorable diversified futures or stock-panel result does not imply favorable performance for every single ETF.
A classifier's positive sentiment or win probability is not an expected return, calibrated utility or portfolio weight.
Papers that motivate a heuristic do not prove that heuristic optimal under this project's different costs and constraints.
A 104-matured-week operational floor is not 104 independent observations when outcomes overlap; effective information and estimation uncertainty remain limited.
Current-news collection is useful prospectively but cannot manufacture original historical news versions or first-receipt timestamps.
bibliographic_notes: DSR is the 2014 Special 40th Anniversary Issue, volume 40(5), DOI 10.3905/jpm.2014.40.5.094.

Novy-Marx is cited under the verified 2015 NBER title Backtesting Strategies Based on Multiple Signals. A related 2016 presentation used Testing Strategies Based on Multiple Signals; no unverified journal year is asserted.
For several journal works, the accessible version read is an earlier author preprint; each entry states the version/access scope. Full inaccessible journal text is not claimed as read.

Faber's 2007 journal citation is verified, but the author-hosted document read is the February 2013 update. Its historical results and same-close assumptions are not represented as the original 2007 experiment or this project's execution model.
RiskMetrics is a corporate-author institutional technical document, not an empirical alpha paper. Daily lambda 0.94 does not endorse a profitable ETF sizing strategy.
Lo (2002) supports dependence-sensitive interpretation; it does not validate the chosen bootstrap block length, exact 225-comparison family or the complete model-selection process.
proposal_vs_implementation: The eight initial review suggestions are not the executed v3 menu. config/experiments_v3.json predeclares sixteen variants. v3_hypothesis_evidence.json maps those actual IDs; unimplemented suggestions (for example ridge) remain proposals.

targeted_additions.reason: Direct provenance for the ten-month trend control, daily EWMA lambda 0.94, and Sharpe dependence/annualization interpretation
